children: , the global payments network, advanced approximately 0.7% to $369.65 Friday as it teamed up with Mastercard
, the rival card-processing network, and Ant International to build shared identity standards for AI purchasing agents. Mastercard shares added 0.4% to $567.59.

The proposed Know-Your-Agent framework aims to give card networks, digital wallets, online marketplaces and AI platforms a common way to verify legitimate agents without surrendering their own approval and fraud controls. The initiative combines Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol, Mastercard Verifiable Intent and Ant's Agentic Mobile Protocol through a platform convened by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

The valuation picture looks appealing: Visa's $369.65 share price sits 13.06% below its GF Value estimate of $425.18. Shared verification could cut friction and help AI-driven shopping scale faster, potentially pushing more transactions across Visa's network. But investors still have only the blueprintno launch date, revenue forecast or new pricing model. The real payoff arrives only if trusted AI agents generate more spending, not simply more technical standards.

title: Visa Stock Rises as AI Alliance Forms, Trades 13.06% Below GF Value
